summary: US-P2: A price resolves deterministically through the hierarchy, with visible provenance
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** a price to resolve through venue → event → series → slot
→ ticket type with explicit overrides, **so that** I can set a house rule once and bend it where I
need to — and always see which level won.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-150 ✅ (closed — shape decided in
[ADR-036](docs/adr/ADR-036-pricing-rules-representation.md))

This is TKT-5's headline COS: *a price resolves deterministically through the hierarchy with
visible provenance (which level won)*. Static, time-invariant rules only — effective windows are
**entirely** TKT-152's (columns *and* filter), and the sale path is TKT-153's.

> **ACs re-synced to the spike's decision** (`decomposition.md` § spike-amended scope). Two changed
> — the ticket-type selector is gone, and the window columns moved to TKT-152. See the
> `kind=claim` comment for the before/after and why.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A migration adds `price_rules` in ADR-036 §3's shape: `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002),
  polymorphic `(scope_level, scope_id)`, `action_kind='absolute'`, `amount bigint CHECK (amount >= 0
  AND amount <= 9007199254740991)` + `currency`, `priority`, `force_ancestor_override`. **No
  `effective_from`/`effective_until`** — those are TKT-152's, with their filter. **No ticket-type
  selector.** Index `price_rules_scope (organizer_id, scope_level, scope_id)`, plain `CREATE INDEX`
  (ADR-020).
- [ ] Resolution is **deterministic and total**: for any (ticket type, context) exactly one rule
  wins, or none does and the ticket type's own `price_amount`/`currency` is the answer —
  **existing data with no rules resolves to today's price, unchanged.**
- [ ] The comparator implements ADR-036 §4 steps 1 and 3–6 (step 2, the window filter, is a no-op
  until TKT-152 and must be *written* so TKT-152 is purely additive). The specificity order is
  `ticket_type > slot > series > event > venue`; a `force_ancestor_override` rule inverts it for
  the forced partition; same-level ties break on `priority` then on lowest `id` — never on row
  order or `ORDER BY` luck.
- [ ] Resolution reports **provenance** per ADR-036 §5: winner (id, scope level, action, priority,
  forced) **and every losing candidate with its reason** from the closed enum. `candidates`
  excludes the winner. A test asserts the **losers** are reported, not just the winner.
- [ ] The truth-table rows ADR-036 §4 assigns to **TKT-151** all pass, via the pure seam
  `SelectPricingRule(at, candidates) RuleSelection` — table-driven, fixed instants and UUIDs, no
  database. Includes the **scope-id collision poison row** and the `forced_ancestor` vs
  `excluded_by_forced_rule` vs `lower_forced_scope` distinction.
- [ ] A currency mismatch between a rule and the ticket type **fails the resolution loudly** — it
  is never silently skipped (ADR-036 §2 / §4 step 1).
- [ ] Catalog exposes resolution as an operation **declared in its OpenAPI document** (not a
  hand-mounted `/internal/` route — ADR-036 §6 explains why that distinction is load-bearing);
  `openapi_gen.go` and `api-types.gen.ts` regenerated **and committed before the gate runs**
  (ADR-009); the operation covered in `services/catalog/internal/api/coverage_test.go` (ADR-030 —
  catalog is out of the smoke gate); response declares **`Cache-Control: no-store`** (ADR-036 §6).
- [ ] The rule lookup is **index-backed**, with ADR-019's two tests: a **poison-row result-scope**
  test *and* an `EXPLAIN`-under-`force_generic_plan` **scan** assertion over the production query
  constant. `explainGenericPlan` takes one parameter today — **generalize it in place**, do not
  fork it. Seed and `ANALYZE` so a sequential scan is the *expensive* choice.

Quality gates: `make check` green (lint + unit + integration, mirrors CI); contract tests for any
touched service boundary (OpenAPI drift check, ADR-009); public-read stories declare their ADR-004
TTL tier with rationale; entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002); money is integer minor units +
ISO-4217 code, floats banned (ADR-001).

objective.note: Organizers set pricing policy at the level it belongs to and override it locally; today the only price is a flat per-ticket-type amount.

scope.note: IN: rule storage, deterministic resolution, provenance, catalog read endpoint. OUT: time windows (TKT-152), commerce wiring (TKT-153), fees/promos/taxes (TKT-6/TKT-32), back-office UI.

uncertainties.note: Closed by TKT-150: ADR-036 fixes the rule shape, conflict semantics and provenance. ACs re-synced to it at claim (see kind=claim).

approach.note: New migration in services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/; resolver as a pure function over loaded rules (the test seam — table-driven, no DB); postgres.go does the scoped fetch; api/server.go exposes it. Mirrors the existing store/postgres/api split.

first_slice.note: Static hierarchy resolution end-to-end (schema → resolver → API → tests) is demoable alone: post rules at two levels, read back which won.

success.note: COS-1 of TKT-5, proven by the loser-reporting test and the no-rule-fallback test.

context_memo.note: Baked below; governingAdrs resolved from docs/adr/ at 2026-07-30 and to be re-resolved at claim time.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.
Commit regenerated code (openapi_gen.go, api-types.gen.ts) before running the gate — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.
Every public read endpoint declares its ADR-004 TTL tier from birth.

governingAdrs.why: THIS TICKET'S SPECIFICATION. §1 scope levels + order, §2 action shape and amount bounds, §3 storage/query/index + append-mostly, §4 the six-step comparator and the truth-table rows owned by TKT-151, §5 the provenance object and its closed reason enum, §6 catalog as the single pricing authority + no-store. Landed after this mémo was first baked.

AMENDED by ADR-036 on the pricing row: rule-based unit-price resolution is now CATALOG's, not commerce's. The mémo's original line said the opposite — do not follow it. Everything else in the five-service cut is unchanged.
Money is integer minor units + ISO-4217; floats banned. Bounds the amount column and forbids any float in the comparator.
Contract-first: this ticket adds a DECLARED operation, so regenerate openapi_gen.go / api-types.gen.ts and COMMIT them before running the gate — check-generate diffs against HEAD.
The new migration runs out-of-band via the binary's migrate subcommand as a one-shot Compose job; the server path never migrates.
The new read declares a tier. ADR-036 §6 already decided it: no-store, because a resolved price feeds a money decision.

Two tests, not one: a poison-row result-scope test AND an EXPLAIN-under-force_generic_plan scan assertion over the production query constant. explainGenericPlan takes one parameter — generalize it in place, do not fork it.
Plain CREATE INDEX. CONCURRENTLY is still not adopted; do not 'improve' the migration.
Catalog is OUT of the smoke happy-path coverage gate — cover the new operation in services/catalog/internal/api/coverage_test.go, not in smoke.
If the plan claims the rule trail is auditable: say honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence. ADR-036 §3 already words this correctly — reuse that wording.

reference.summary: Today's price is a single `price_amount` column on `ticket_types` (migration 0001); commerce reads it via catalog's `/internal/ticket-types/{id}`.
ADR-019's worked examples (TKT-53, TKT-60) are the shape of the scoping evidence this ticket owes.
ADR-036 §4 carries the 19-row truth table with an owner column; the rows marked TKT-151 are this ticket's test suite.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-151

**Gate 1 waived** for this run (epic TKT-5's `kind=claim` waiver): the agent performed
`Backlog → Ready` as the owner's proxy.

**Selection reason.** Its only blocker, TKT-150, closed — verified from the board, not from
memory. It is now the sole claimable child of TKT-5: TKT-152 and TKT-153 are both `blocked-by`
this ticket. Highest unblocking power in the epic (closing it unblocks the remaining two).

**Not `risk:low`.** Re-checked, not assumed: a new migration, a new contract-declared operation,
regenerated artefacts in two languages, and the pricing semantics every later money path consumes.
The plan gate applies — resolved under the Gate 2 waiver, with every self-made decision recorded in
`kind=plan-final`.

---

#### ACs re-synced to TKT-150's decision (`decomposition.md` § spike-amended scope)

The spike narrowed this ticket in two ways. Doing this **now**, before Planning, rather than
letting the planner re-litigate a contradiction:

| # | Was (pre-spike AC) | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "one row per (scope level, scope id, **ticket-type selector**)" | **No selector.** A rule at scope X applies to every ticket type beneath X; to price one tier differently, author a `ticket_type`-scoped rule. | `ticket_types.performance_id` makes ticket types **per-performance**, so there is no stable cross-performance tier identity for a venue-scoped rule's selector to name. The column could only ever match one row — which is what a `ticket_type`-scoped rule already is. A cross-performance tier identity is owed by a future catalog story. |
| 2 | (implicit) the rule table carries its effective window | **Window columns move to TKT-152**, together with the filter. | Splitting them would let TKT-151 store a timed rule its own resolver ignores — and all-`NULL` tests pass whether or not the filter exists, so nothing would catch it. ADR-036 §4 assigns each truth-table row an owner for exactly this reason. |

Three ACs were also **sharpened** rather than changed: the amount bound (`<= 9007199254740991`,
matching `Money.amount` — ADR-036 §2), the `(scope_level, scope_id)` **pair** predicate with its
poison-row test (matching on `scope_id` alone loads foreign-scope rules — ADR-036 §3), and the
`no-store` cache tier as a correctness argument rather than a performance one (ADR-036 §6).

#### Context-mémo revalidated at pickup, not trusted

The mémo was baked at decomposition (`capturedAt: 2026-07-30`) and **one governing ADR has landed
since**: **ADR-036**, this ticket's own specification. Also **ADR-002 changed** — ADR-036 amended
its pricing row, so the mémo's ADR-002 line ("commerce owns pricing evaluation") is now **stale in
the direction that matters most for this ticket**. Both corrected below. This is exactly the
staleness the `id`+`date`+`capturedAt` fields exist to make detectable (TKT-73, TKT-79).

Branch: `TKT-151-price-rule-hierarchy`.
